items.name: The Ashen Compass
items.description: A device that points toward the nearest act of intentional killing, its needle glowing brighter the closer one gets. Used by investigators and bounty hunters — but also by those who would rather find a murder before it happens.

items.name: The Dying Candle
items.description: A candle that burns with a black, lightless flame only in the presence of someone who has killed within the last year. It casts shadow, not light — a silent confession no one can refuse.

items.name: Veins of Lethe
items.description: A rare mineral found only in the deepest mines that erases the involuntary Death Debt memories of killers. Fiercely sought after, heavily controlled, and rumored to erase more than just memories if used too often.

items.name: The Mourner's Bell
items.description: A bell that, when rung, causes everyone who hears it to feel the emotional state of the most recently killed person. Used in funeral rites across Aeternum — sacred to some, torture to others.

items.name: The Fleshward
items.description: An alchemical salve that temporarily restores a scarred or mutilated body to its original Stillness-day appearance for one agonizing day. The most counterfeited substance in Aeternum's black markets.

items.name: The Tallybone
items.description: A piece of carved bone worn by Death Wardens, each notch representing a sanctioned kill. It is simultaneously a badge of authority, a record of service, and an unerasable confession of every life taken.

events.name: The Night of a Thousand Silences
events.description: A single night in which one thousand people were killed simultaneously across the capital. The collective silence was so profound it permanently deafened half the city. The event haunts Aeternum as the night silence became a weapon.

events.name: The Child Uprising
events.description: Children frozen at young ages for centuries rose against adult-bodied immortals, demanding the right to grow. They were brutally suppressed. Their youngest leaders still sit in prison cells — forever seven years old.

events.name: The Scar Epidemic
events.description: A sadistic cult deliberately mutilated thousands of people, knowing their bodies would never heal the marks. Those scars remain on living bodies today, a visible wound that time cannot mend and society cannot forget.

events.name: The Great Refusal
events.description: A movement where millions voluntarily surrendered the power to kill simultaneously, nearly collapsing the sanctioned-death system. The constitutional crisis it triggered remains unresolved to this day.

events.name: The Memory Flood
events.description: A Warden's vault cracked, spilling centuries of bottled Death Debts into the water supply. An entire district experienced the memories of thousands of murdered people at once. Many went permanently mad; the district is still quarantined.

events.name: The Census of the Damned
events.description: A recent and controversial recount revealed far more living people than anyone admitted, and far fewer sanctioned deaths than births — threatening the fragile arithmetic that keeps Aeternum's civilization from collapsing under its own eternal weight.

premise.stakes: If the truth of mortality spreads, the fragile arithmetic revealed by the Census of the Damned becomes irrelevant — people will no longer need sanctioned killing to leave existence, collapsing the entire power structure of Aeternum. But if Marchand buries it, Sera loses the only evidence that her own suffering — centuries of killing and carrying the dead — might one day end naturally. Either way, her identity may not survive the choice.
premise.logline: When the Ashen Compass goes dark for the first time in seven centuries, a Death Warden drowning in borrowed memories discovers a body that aged to death — and must hide the miracle from the regime that would kill to keep immortality the only law.
premise.fatalFlaw: Sera's accumulated Death Debts have eroded her sense of self so thoroughly that she doubts her own memories and instincts. She cannot trust her own mind — and as the investigation demands sharper judgment than ever, her fracturing identity makes her vulnerable to manipulation and increasingly dependent on Veins of Lethe, the very substance Marchand controls.
tenPointsPlan: OPEN: Sera Voss investigates a routine sanctioned killing — a standard Warden's day — but the Ashen Compass in her hand suddenly stops working mid-case, going dark for the first time in her centuries of service.

Sera is summoned to a secondary scene: a body found in a tenement with no wounds, no scars, no evidence of violence. The person appears to have simply... aged. Neighbors say the victim was fine yesterday. The Dying Candle in the room burns normally — no one nearby has killed.

Sera consults the Tallybone records and discovers the victim had no sanctioned death warrant, no enemies of note, and was registered as age forty-three for over six hundred years. The Silence of the Dying never fell. By every law of Aeternum, this death is impossible.

Sera's accumulated Death Debts flare — a dead victim's memory surfaces unbidden, mixing with the crime scene, making her doubt what she's seeing. She reaches for Veins of Lethe to clear her mind, but her supplier tells her the mines have restricted all distribution on High Warden Marchand's orders.

Marchand appears at the scene, preemptively, before Sera even reports her findings. He confiscates the body under ancient authority, citing a containment protocol that hasn't been invoked since the Memory Flood. He tells Sera the case is closed — natural causes, rare anomaly, no further inquiry.

Sera disobeys. She visits the quarantined Memory Flood district seeking a rogue alchemist who once studied the Stillness itself, navigating streets full of people still experiencing fragments of thousands of murdered memories — a landscape of perpetual psychic torment.

The alchemist reveals a theory: the Stillness was never permanent. It was a pause — and like any paused breath, it must eventually resume. The body Sera found may be the first to start aging again. If true, the Stillness is ending, and with it, every institution built on eternal life.

Marchand's agents ambush Sera in the quarantine zone. A fight erupts — Sera kills one agent in self-defense, triggering the Silence of the Dying and inheriting the agent's final memory: a glimpse of Marchand's private vault, filled with dozens of bodies showing the same impossible aging. This isn't the first case. It's the latest in a pattern he's been hiding.

Sera returns to Warden headquarters to find Marchand has formally charged her with unsanctioned killing and stripped her Tallybone. She is now a fugitive — hunted by the very system she served, carrying a dead agent's memory of a secret that could unravel civilization.

CLIFFHANGER: Sera, cornered and out of options, rings a Mourner's Bell in a crowded square — forcing hundreds of civilians to feel the emotional state of the impossible victim. The crowd experiences something none of them have ever felt: the quiet, natural peace of a death that was not murder. The episode ends on the question hanging in the air — is this terror, or is this hope?
premise.antagonistMove: Theocratic faction leader High Warden Cael Marchand — who controls the Veins of Lethe mines and has built his power on the monopoly of death — recognizes that if death-by-aging is real and spreading, the entire economy of killing collapses. He begins quietly eliminating anyone who has touched the body or learned the truth, using sanctioned kills under fabricated warrants to bury the evidence before it can destabilize his regime.
premise.protagonistHook: [Sera Voss][char-20d82216] has carried so many [Death Debts][rule-the-death-debt] that her own childhood is indistinguishable from the hundreds of strangers who died by her hand — she keeps a journal just to remember her real name. When she's called to a tenement where a body lies without wound, scar, or the [Silence of the Dying][rule-the-silence-of-the-dying], her [Ashen Compass][item-the-ashen-compass] spins like a compass dropped at sea: no intentional killing occurred, and the instrument has no category for what happened. For the first time in seven centuries of [Warden][item-the-tallybone] service, Sera faces a death that no one caused — a miracle her training frames as a threat, and her fracturing mind can't trust enough to dismiss.
premise.thematicQuestion: If death is the only economy, the only law, and the only escape — what happens to a civilization that discovers it might one day be free of all three?
premise.inevitableConsequence: If Sera follows the truth to its source, she will have to choose between a world where death-by-aging frees everyone from the economy of killing — including freeing her from the Death Debts that are slowly erasing her — and a world where she sides with the Wardens to suppress the miracle and preserve the only order anyone has ever known, condemning herself to centuries more of borrowed memories and fractured selfhood.

worldRules.consequence: Every life taken must be weighed against a life given. No death is free; the universe demands balance, creating an economy of killing where every murder has a price.
When a person is killed, all sound within ten paces ceases for exactly one breath. This silence is the soul's departure and the world's only acknowledgment of death.
Killers involuntarily inherit a fragment of their victim's memories. This debt cannot be refused, refused, or willed away, making every kill a permanent psychic burden.
A person about to be killed may speak one final sentence magically bound to be heard by the killer. No one can refuse the Last Word, and some have toppled regimes with theirs.
Every scar, wound, and mutilation accumulates across centuries of immortality, healing only in function, never in appearance. Bodies become living records of every violence endured.
Each person is frozen at the biological age they were when the Stillness struck. Children remain children forever, elders remain elders, and apparent age reveals nothing about power or experience.

storyPlan.worldDescription:
Seven centuries ago, the biological clock of every living person in Aeternum simply stopped. No aging. No sickness. No decay. The event — never explained, never repeated — is called the Stillness, and it remade civilization in a single breath. Bodies persist. Wounds knit in function but never in form, because [The Flesh Remembers][rule-the-flesh-remembers] every violence endured across centuries: a stab wound from four hundred years ago still weeps its shadow on living skin, and the scarred walk among the unscarred as living testimony to what they survived. Each person was locked at the age they occupied when the Stillness struck — [The Age Lock][rule-the-age-lock] means a child of seven remains seven forever, and an elder of eighty walks hunched through eternity, so that apparent age in Aeternum reveals nothing about power, wisdom, or suffering. A twelve-year-old may have ruled a province for five hundred years. A grandmother's body may house a mind only decades old. No one trusts the face.

The only exit from existence is deliberate killing by another hand. This singular truth reshaped every institution, economy, and belief into instruments of death. The founding principle is [The Law of Equivalence][rule-the-law-of-equivalence]: every life taken must be weighed against a life given, so no death is free, and murder has a price — sometimes paid in currency, sometimes in another corpse, sometimes in something far worse. When a kill occurs, [The Silence of the Dying][rule-the-silence-of-the-dying] falls — all sound within ten paces ceases for exactly one breath, the soul's departure and the world's only acknowledgment of what was done. That silence is sacred and feared; on the [Night of a Thousand Silences][event-the-night-of-a-thousand-silences], one thousand people were killed simultaneously across the capital, and the collective silence was so profound it permanently deafened half the city. Aeternum remembers it as the night silence itself became a weapon.

The killer pays a price of their own. Through [The Death Debt][rule-the-death-debt], every killer involuntarily inherits a fragment of their victim's memories — an unpayable, inescapable obligation that accumulates across a lifetime of killing and slowly fills the murderer's mind with the dead. Those who carry too many Death Debts seek out [Veins of Lethe][item-veins-of-lethe], a rare mineral mined only in the deepest pits that erases inherited murder-memories — though the mining rights are controlled by the very Wardens who cause the debt, and rumor persists that Lethe erases more than just memories when used too often. The dying, meanwhile, hold one final weapon: [The Last Word][rule-the-last-word], a single sentence magically bound to be heard by the killer, impossible to refuse, and some Last Words have toppled regimes from beyond the grave.

Aeternum governs killing through Death Wardens — sanctioned killers whose authority is etched into [The Tallybone][item-the-tallybone], a carved bone recording every sanctioned life they have taken, simultaneously badge of office, ledger of service, and unerasable confession. Investigators and bounty hunters navigate the after-math of murder with [The Ashen Compass][item-the-ashen-compass], whose needle swings toward the nearest act of intentional killing and glows brighter with proximity. In every Warden's chamber burns [The Dying Candle][item-the-dying-candle], a candle that casts shadow instead of light whenever someone who has killed within the last year stands near — a silent, inescapable confession. At funerals across the world, [The Mourner's Bell][item-the-mourner's-bell] is struck, and all who hear it are forced to feel the emotional state of the most recently killed person, a ritual of compelled empathy that some find sacred and others find torturous. For the vain and the ashamed, the black markets offer [The Fleshward][item-the-fleshward], an alchemical salve that temporarily restores a scarred body to its Stillness-day appearance for a single agonizing day — the most counterfeited substance in Aeternum.

History is written in acts of killing that reshaped the world. The [Child Uprising][event-the-child-uprising] saw children frozen at young ages for hundreds of years rise against adult-bodied immortals, demanding the right to grow; they were brutally suppressed, and their youngest leaders still sit in prison cells, forever seven years old, forever furious. The [Scar Epidemic][event-the-scar-epidemic] followed, when a sadistic cult deliberately mutilated thousands, knowing their bodies would never heal — those scars persist on living flesh today, a wound time cannot mend. In defiance, the [Great Refusal][event-the-great-refusal] was a mass movement where millions voluntarily surrendered the power to kill, nearly collapsing the sanctioned-death system and forcing a constitutional crisis that smolders unresolved to this day. The catastrophe known as the [Memory Flood][event-the-memory-flood] occurred when a Warden's vault cracked and centuries of bottled Death Debts spilled into the water supply, causing an entire district to experience the memories of thousands of murdered people at once — many went permanently mad, and the district remains quarantined behind walls no one has touched in a century. Most recently, the [Census of the Damned][event-the-census-of-the-damned] counted the living and found far more than anyone admitted, and far fewer sanctioned deaths than births, threatening the fragile arithmetic that keeps Aeternum's civilization from collapsing under its own eternal, accumulating weight.

In Aeternum, death is not the end of life. It is the only economy, the only law, and the only escape — and everyone knows it.
